title: Macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's eye condition.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for vision screening.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman who presents for a routine ophthalmology evaluation. She has a known history of type 2 diabetes. She reports no acute changes in her vision or new ocular symptoms since her last visit. She is here today for a baseline screening of her retinal health.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily
Amlodipine 5mg daily

Exam
Visual acuity is stable. Funduscopic examination of the right eye reveals mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy. There is no evidence of significant complications or surrounding changes in the retinal architecture.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes
2. Mild NPDR of the right eye

Plan
The patient will continue her current medications for blood pressure and cholesterol management. We will monitor her glucose levels closely. A follow-up appointment will be scheduled in 12 months for a repeat retinal exam.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes with mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy without macular edema, right eye: E11.3291 (HCC 37 only).

distractors.why: The type and severity of retinopathy are documented.
